correctness.rationale: PASS. The claim quantifies over every induced nonattacking-rook matching complex of a subset B of at most 16 positions in the 5-by-5 board, modulo separate row/column permutations; it does not claim arbitrary larger subboards. I independently rebuilt the complete 5-row bitmask canonicalization, enumerated 5130 distinct row/column orbit representatives of cardinality 0..16 (k=0..16 counts 1,1,3,6,16,34,69,130,234,367,527,669,755,755,669,527,367), and reconstructed the matching-complex integral boundary d3. Exactly 1 of 367 size-16 types has a nonunit residual: representative (3,13,28,30,30), 161 triangles,108 tetrahedra, 93 integral unit pivots and a single column with 24 nonzero entries all of absolute value 3. Every other type gives no third-boundary torsion. The original package additionally checks mod3 ranks d2=67,d3=93 for that board, d2=176,d3=423 for the full 5-by-5 board, and nonzero ambient inclusion, with exact boundary witnesses. The independently reconstructed exhaustive finite state space certifies this bounded classification; absence of a smaller board is not inferred from timeouts. The order-three group on the witness and ambient inclusion depend on exact integer boundary and mod3 cycle arguments, not merely on saved VERIFY_OK logs.

value.rationale: PASS. The 5-by-5 complete chessboard complex is the first natural square chessboard with second-degree 3-torsion. Locating the smallest induced board on which that torsion exists intrinsically (not just as a chain supported in the large board), establishing uniqueness up to its natural S5 × S5 symmetry, and showing that its inclusion detects the global torsion are sharp, motivated boundaries in matching-complex topology. The invariant is not an arbitrary slice, a table recomputation, or a routine consequence of the known full-board homology. Limits: 5-by-5 subboards of cardinality at most 16 and specific degree two; not a classification of all boards or higher homology.
